sources.entry: Algo - Personal IPSEC VPN in the cloud. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/trailofbits/algo)

summary.one_liner: Algo VPN is a set of Ansible scripts that deploy a personal WireGuard and IPsec VPN server onto a new cloud virtual machine or an existing Ubuntu server.
summary.what_it_does: Algo runs Ansible playbooks from your local machine (or Google Cloud Shell) to provision an Ubuntu 22.04 LTS server with a WireGuard and IPsec VPN. You list the users in config.cfg and the scripts generate per-user configs: WireGuard .conf files and QR codes for iOS, macOS, Android and Windows, plus IPsec certificates and Apple profiles. Helper commands add or remove users later via update-users. Optional features include a local DNS resolver that blocks ads, limited SSH tunneling users, and privacy settings such as log rotation and minimal logging. The README says IPsec is limited to IKEv2 with AES-GCM, SHA2 and P-256, and that legacy protocols like L2TP, IKEv1 and OpenVPN are not installed.
use_cases: Set up a personal VPN server in the cloud
Route phone and laptop traffic through a server you control
Create WireGuard configs and QR codes for several devices
Auto-configure iOS or macOS built-in IPsec VPN
Add or remove VPN users after deployment
Tunnel browser traffic through an SSH SOCKS proxy
how_to_run: Edit config.cfg and list the users in the users list
Import the generated files from the configs/ directory into your VPN client
notable: Deploys a fresh VM to many cloud providers, or to your own Ubuntu server
Generates Apple IPsec profiles so iOS and macOS need no third-party client for IPsec
Optional local DNS resolver for ad blocking
Optional SSH-only tunneling accounts with no shell access
Privacy controls: log rotation after 7 days and a privacy-monitor script
caveats: IPsec user management requires choosing to retain the PKI keys during deployment, and the p12 and CA passwords are shown only once
Some settings such as cloud provider and other options should be set before deployment, since changing them later may require a new server
The README says it does not claim anonymity or censorship avoidance, and perfect privacy is impossible
